content.user_title: Generate Typed UI Code from Render Specs
content.value_statement: Turning UI specifications into maintainable application code can require repetitive traversal and prop serialization. This skill provides reusable utilities for generating structured code and custom exporters from json-render specifications.
actual_capabilities: Generate code from json-render UI specifications.
Traverse nested UI specification trees recursively.
Serialize component properties for generated output.
Build custom exporters for different application targets.
Format traversal output with component types and nesting.
limitations: It does not design UI specifications without an input schema.
Generated output still requires review, formatting, and project integration.
It does not guarantee compatibility with every framework or runtime.
It does not replace tests for generated application code.

use_cases.title: Prototype UI Exporters
use_cases.description: Create an exporter that converts structured UI specifications into a format used by a prototype application.

use_cases.title: Inspect Component Trees
use_cases.description: Traverse nested render specifications to inspect component types, hierarchy, and serialized properties during development.

use_cases.title: Build Production Generators
use_cases.description: Extend the code generation pipeline with a custom target that produces consistent application code from approved UI specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what this code generation utility does, which input specification it expects, and what output it produces.

prompt_templates.title: Traverse a UI Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this json-render UI specification, describe its component hierarchy and list each component type in traversal order.

prompt_templates.title: Serialize Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the supplied component properties into stable generated-output values, preserving nested structures and documenting unsupported values.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Exporter
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom exporter for the specified target framework. Define traversal behavior, prop serialization rules, formatting decisions, unsupported cases, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A nested dashboard specification containing panels, headings, data tables, and action controls.
output_examples.output: A traversal summary that lists each component type in hierarchy order and identifies the nesting depth of every element.

output_examples.input: A component specification with strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and nested property values.
output_examples.output: A normalized property representation suitable for insertion into generated application code, with unsupported values clearly identified.

output_examples.input: A request for an exporter targeting a custom component runtime.
output_examples.output: An exporter design covering tree traversal, component mapping, property serialization, output formatting, and validation responsibilities.

best_practices: Validate the input specification before generating output.
Define explicit mappings for supported components and property types.
Review and test generated code within the target application.
anti_patterns: Treating generated output as production-ready without review.
Accepting arbitrary property values without serialization rules.
Adding target-specific behavior without exporter-level tests.

faq.question: What input does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a json-render UI specification or a compatible structured component tree.

faq.question: Can it generate code for any framework?
faq.answer: It supports custom exporters, but each framework needs explicit component mappings and output rules.

faq.question: Does it create the UI design?
faq.answer: No. It transforms an existing specification and does not replace product or interface design work.

faq.question: Can it serialize nested properties?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides utilities for traversing specifications and serializing structured component properties.

faq.question: Is generated output ready to deploy?
faq.answer: No. Review, formatting, integration, and tests remain necessary before deployment.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Frontend developers, design systems engineers, and teams building repeatable UI generation pipelines.
